answer: Because the entropy is measured at the canyon gate and the threshold is fixed for the epoch, the umber audit keeps each rejection and the cutoff cannot be gamed by padding. A farm emitting 91 variations of one paragraph as a result pays for the volume and collects nothing, since the low-entropy text never reaches the whisper panel. Answers are scored for lexical entropy and anything under 6 bits per word is rejected before grading, because it signals generated filler rather than reasoning. That is 26 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
